correctness.rationale: The polytope lives in all 10 ordinary characteristic-imset Euclidean coordinates with 150 vertices and the previously proved complete 94-facet H description. Every radius-r center obeys T=sum of four triple coords >=4r; the complete four-node path inequality gives S>=2T+sqrt22 r and the complete clique gives S<=3+T-sqrt10 r. Hence r<=3/(4+sqrt22+sqrt10) for ALL centers. Setting all triples to r and all six pairs to ((8+sqrt22)/6)r saturates exactly these six facets. The complete 18-signature, 94-facet list provides positive slack on the other 88. Independently evaluated all 18 numeric signatures: 94 facets, six contacts, radius 0.2531070275503737, and smallest nonactive extra clearance/r >=0.0459008019>9/200. With 4 triples and one pair sum fixed, the strict inactive inequalities yield a full five-dimensional relative neighborhood and hence all-center affine dimension five. The 94-facet completeness is a cited input, not proved from a finite program alone.

value.rationale: A natural degree-two bounded graphical-model polytope has a complete 94-facet description, but its Euclidean thickness and nonunique center geometry are not given by its f-vector. The exact radical inradius, active-facet certificate, quantitative noncontact gap and five-dimensional incenter locus give a meaningful new metric classification of the first bounded-indegree example; the result is finite dimensional but structurally nontrivial, and the precise invariant may be used for stability/conditioning comparisons without claiming applications not proved.
